pr.title: Port the administration tools to .NET 10 and bundle the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime
pr.body:
## Summary

Phase 0c1 of the modernization roadmap. The **administration tools move from .NET Framework 4.5 to .NET 10 LTS** (supported until 2028-11-14), and the **installer bundles the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime**.

Tools ported: Administrator, DBSetup, DBSetupQuick, DBUpdater, DataDirectorySynchronizer, Shared and GenerateComApiDocumentation. The test projects follow in 0c2, together with NUnit 4.

## Projects

- SDK-style `net10.0-windows` projects. These are kept exactly as before:
  - item lists
  - assembly names
  - icons
  - project references
  - `bin\x64\<Configuration>` output paths
- `AssemblyInfo.cs` keeps the stamped version, and the SDK generates the platform attributes.
- `System.ServiceProcess.ServiceController` 10.0.13 comes from NuGet. DirectoryServices is part of the Windows Desktop runtime.
- `Interop.hMailServer.targets` now works for SDK projects:
  - it no longer depends on `IntermediateOutputPath`
  - it finds TlbImp through the Windows SDK registry key
  - it stamps ArzoieMail as the interop's product and company

## Behavior kept the same

| .NET change | Handling |
|---|---|
| WinForms analyzer `WFO1000` (.NET 9+) | 18 custom-control and dialog properties declare `DesignerSerializationVisibility.Visible`, which is what the designer did implicitly |
| `Process.Start(url)` no longer goes through the shell | Links open through a new `ShellLauncher` (`UseShellExecute`) |
| The executing assembly is `hMailAdmin.dll`, not the `.exe` | Restarting after a language change uses `Environment.ProcessPath` |
| The default font changed to Segoe UI 9pt | The forms keep Microsoft Sans Serif 8.25pt, which they are laid out for |
| `Rijndael` is obsolete | Replaced by `Aes` (same cipher). **A password saved by the .NET Framework build was confirmed to decrypt on .NET 10.** A saved password that can't be decrypted now prompts instead of throwing. |

## Installer and CI

- Setup **bundles** Microsoft's `windowsdesktop-runtime-10.0.13-win-x64.exe` (60 MB). It's fetched by the new `libraries\fetch-dotnet-runtime.ps1` and checked against Microsoft's published SHA-512.
- Setup installs it silently when it's missing, before any tool runs. Exit codes 3010 (reboot needed) and 1638 (newer version present) count as success. This replaces the .NET Framework 4.5 check.
- Detection uses `Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App\10.*` (where the .NET host resolves the runtime) or the **32-bit** registry view. The .NET installers record x64 runtimes there, which the first version of this PR missed.
- Each tool is installed with its `.dll`, `.deps.json`, `.runtimeconfig.json` and `.dll.config`. Stale `.exe.config` files are removed on upgrade.
- CI:
  - caches the runtime installer
  - builds the tools with `/restore`
  - drops the .NET Framework targeting-pack fallback
  - adds the tools' `.dll` files to the signing list

## Tests

New `Infrastructure\DotNetTools` regression tests check:
- each tool's installed .NET files
- that the tools target `Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App` 10
- that no `.exe.config` files remain
- that a .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is installed, plus its 32-bit registry registration

✅ CI [Build run](https://github.com/jassifx/arzoiemail/actions/runs/40074064839): **1,185 passed, 0 failed**. That's the baseline of 1,174 plus 11 new tests, all passing. Inconclusive (34) and skipped (75) are unchanged. The installer also compiles locally (65.9 MB).

## Not covered by CI

- The CI image already has .NET 10, so setup skips the bundled runtime there. The install path itself is exercised by the VMTestRunner's clean Windows environments.
- The SignPath "binaries" artifact configuration will need the tools' `.dll` entries once signing is set up for ArzoieMail.

+<#
+.SYNOPSIS
+    Fetches the .NET Desktop Runtime installer that the ArzoieMail setup bundles.
+
+.DESCRIPTION
+    The administration tools (hMailAdmin, DBSetup, DBUpdater, ...) are .NET 10 Windows Forms
+    applications and need the .NET Desktop Runtime. The setup program carries Microsoft's
+    runtime installer and runs it when the runtime is missing, so that an installation needs
+    no internet connection.
+
+    Downloads windowsdesktop-runtime-<Version>-win-x64.exe from Microsoft into
+    %hMailServerLibs%\dotnet-desktop-runtime-<Version>, and verifies it against the SHA-512
+    pinned below. Like 7-Zip, it is shipped as downloaded, so a substituted file would go
+    straight to every installation; an unlisted version is refused.
+
+    Prerequisites:
+      - The environment variable hMailServerLibs, pointing at your library folder.
+
+.PARAMETER Version
+    The .NET Desktop Runtime version to fetch, e.g. 10.0.13. Must be listed in $RuntimeHashes.
+
+.EXAMPLE
+    powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File libraries\fetch-dotnet-runtime.ps1 -Version 10.0.13
+#>
+[CmdletBinding()]
+param(
+    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
+    [ValidatePattern('^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$')]
+    [string]$Version
+)
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
+
+# SHA-512 of each supported windowsdesktop-runtime-<version>-win-x64.exe, as Microsoft
+# publishes it in the release metadata:
+#
+#     https://builds.dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet/release-metadata/10.0/releases.json
+#     -> releases[].windowsdesktop.files[] where rid == win-x64 and name ends in .exe -> hash
+#
+# Add an entry here when pinning a new version.
+$RuntimeHashes = @{
+    "10.0.13" = "ADAF5E06B66B145848F3A994B51EA1590D19A5C02F6E7C5899ED896BBDB020AF6386D2EAEF613034D697388ADAF48AA8C3291343F0BBB5F8E62E37AFF9564A00"
+}
+
+# --- Set up a build log ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+. (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath "build-common.ps1")
+
+$logPath = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath "fetch-dotnet-runtime.log"
+Start-BuildLog -LogPath $logPath -Title ".NET Desktop Runtime $Version fetch log"
+
+# --- Resolve the library folder -------------------------------------------------
+
+$libsPath = Resolve-HMailServerLibs
+
+if (-not $RuntimeHashes.ContainsKey($Version))
+{
+    $known = ($RuntimeHashes.Keys | Sort-Object) -join ", "
+    Throw "No pinned SHA-512 is recorded for the .NET Desktop Runtime $Version. Known versions: $known. Record it in `$RuntimeHashes in $PSCommandPath from Microsoft's release metadata."
+}
+
+$destDir = Join-Path -Path $libsPath -ChildPath "dotnet-desktop-runtime-$Version"
+$fileName = "windowsdesktop-runtime-$Version-win-x64.exe"
+$url = "https://builds.dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet/WindowsDesktop/$Version/$fileName"
+
+# --- Download and verify --------------------------------------------------------
+
+if (Test-Path $destDir)
+{
+    Write-Log "Removing existing folder $destDir for a clean fetch"
+    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $destDir -Recurse -Force
+}
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $destDir | Out-Null
+
+$target = Join-Path -Path $destDir -ChildPath $fileName
+
+Write-Log "Downloading $url"
+[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
+Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $target
+
+$expectedHash = $RuntimeHashes[$Version]
+$actualHash = (Get-FileHash -Path $target -Algorithm SHA512).Hash
+if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash)
+{
+    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $destDir -Recurse -Force
+    Throw "The SHA-512 of $fileName did not match the pinned value. Expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash. The download was discarded."
+}
+
+Write-Log "SHA-512 verified"
+Write-Log ".NET Desktop Runtime $Version fetched into $target"

commit.message:
Port the administration tools to .NET 10 and bundle the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime

The tools (Administrator, DBSetup, DBSetupQuick, DBUpdater, DataDirectorySynchronizer,
Shared, GenerateComApiDocumentation) move from .NET Framework 4.5 to .NET 10 LTS
(supported until 2028-11-14).

Projects
- SDK-style net10.0-windows projects. Their item lists, assembly names, icons, project
  references and bin\x64\<Configuration> output paths are kept as they were.
- AssemblyInfo.cs keeps the stamped version; the SDK generates the platform attributes.
- System.ServiceProcess.ServiceController comes from NuGet (10.0.13); DirectoryServices is
  part of the Windows Desktop runtime.
- Interop.hMailServer.targets works for SDK projects: it no longer depends on
  IntermediateOutputPath, finds TlbImp through the Windows SDK registry key, and stamps
  ArzoieMail as the interop's product and company.

Code
- WFO1000: the custom controls' and dialogs' public properties declare
  DesignerSerializationVisibility.Visible, which is what the designer did implicitly.
- Links open through ShellLauncher (UseShellExecute), which .NET no longer does by default.
- Restarting the Administrator after a language change uses Environment.ProcessPath; the
  executing assembly is hMailAdmin.dll on .NET.
- The forms keep the .NET Framework default font (Microsoft Sans Serif 8.25pt) they are
  laid out for; .NET changed it to Segoe UI 9pt.
- Rijndael (obsolete) becomes Aes for the Administrator's saved passwords. It is the same
  cipher, and a password saved by the .NET Framework build was confirmed to decrypt. A
  saved password that cannot be decrypted now prompts instead of throwing.

Installer and CI
- Setup bundles Microsoft's windowsdesktop-runtime-10.0.13-win-x64.exe, fetched by the new
  libraries\fetch-dotnet-runtime.ps1 and checked against Microsoft's SHA-512, and installs
  it silently when no .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is present, before any tool is started. This
  replaces the .NET Framework 4.5 check.
- Each tool is installed with its .dll, .deps.json, .runtimeconfig.json and .dll.config;
  stale .exe.config files are removed on upgrade.
- CI caches the runtime installer, builds the tools with /restore, no longer needs the
  .NET Framework targeting-pack fallback, and signs the tools' .dll files as well.

New regression tests (Infrastructure\DotNetTools) check the installed tools' .NET files,
that they target Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 10, that no .exe.config files remain, and
that a .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is installed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Detect the .NET Desktop Runtime where the .NET host finds it

The setup looked for the runtime under the 64-bit registry view, but the .NET installers
record x64 runtimes in the 32-bit view (WOW6432Node), so it never saw an installed
runtime. A runtime installed without a .NET installer, as on the CI image, is not in the
registry at all. The setup now looks for a 10.* folder in
Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App, where the .NET host resolves it
from, and also accepts a 10.x entry in the 32-bit view.

The regression test checks the same folder, and a second one checks the 32-bit
registration when a .NET installer made one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The tools (Administrator, DBSetup, DBSetupQuick, DBUpdater, DataDirectorySynchronizer,
Shared, GenerateComApiDocumentation) move from .NET Framework 4.5 to .NET 10 LTS
(supported until 2028-11-14).

Projects
- SDK-style net10.0-windows projects. Their item lists, assembly names, icons, project
  references and bin\x64\<Configuration> output paths are kept as they were.
- AssemblyInfo.cs keeps the stamped version; the SDK generates the platform attributes.
- System.ServiceProcess.ServiceController comes from NuGet (10.0.13); DirectoryServices is
  part of the Windows Desktop runtime.
- Interop.hMailServer.targets works for SDK projects: it no longer depends on
  IntermediateOutputPath, finds TlbImp through the Windows SDK registry key, and stamps
  ArzoieMail as the interop's product and company.

Code
- WFO1000: the custom controls' and dialogs' public properties declare
  DesignerSerializationVisibility.Visible, which is what the designer did implicitly.
- Links open through ShellLauncher (UseShellExecute), which .NET no longer does by default.
- Restarting the Administrator after a language change uses Environment.ProcessPath; the
  executing assembly is hMailAdmin.dll on .NET.
- The forms keep the .NET Framework default font (Microsoft Sans Serif 8.25pt) they are
  laid out for; .NET changed it to Segoe UI 9pt.
- Rijndael (obsolete) becomes Aes for the Administrator's saved passwords. It is the same
  cipher, and a password saved by the .NET Framework build was confirmed to decrypt. A
  saved password that cannot be decrypted now prompts instead of throwing.

Installer and CI
- Setup bundles Microsoft's windowsdesktop-runtime-10.0.13-win-x64.exe, fetched by the new
  libraries\fetch-dotnet-runtime.ps1 and checked against Microsoft's SHA-512, and installs
  it silently when no .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is present, before any tool is started. This
  replaces the .NET Framework 4.5 check.
- Each tool is installed with its .dll, .deps.json, .runtimeconfig.json and .dll.config;
  stale .exe.config files are removed on upgrade.
- CI caches the runtime installer, builds the tools with /restore, no longer needs the
  .NET Framework targeting-pack fallback, and signs the tools' .dll files as well.

New regression tests (Infrastructure\DotNetTools) check the installed tools' .NET files,
that they target Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 10, that no .exe.config files remain, and
that a .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is installed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Detect the .NET Desktop Runtime where the .NET host finds it

The setup looked for the runtime under the 64-bit registry view, but the .NET installers
record x64 runtimes in the 32-bit view (WOW6432Node), so it never saw an installed
runtime. A runtime installed without a .NET installer, as on the CI image, is not in the
registry at all. The setup now looks for a 10.* folder in
Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App, where the .NET host resolves it
from, and also accepts a 10.x entry in the 32-bit view.

The regression test checks the same folder, and a second one checks the 32-bit
registration when a .NET installer made one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.body:
Phase 0c2 of the modernization: the test solution follows the tools (#7) onto .NET 10.

## What changes

- **RegressionTests, VolumeTests, VMTestRunner.Console** are SDK-style `net10.0-windows` projects. Item lists stay explicit, as in the tools.
- **Package versions** are pinned once, in `hmailserver/test/Directory.Packages.props` (Central Package Management):

  | Package | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | NUnit | 3.13.3 | **5.0.0** |
  | NUnit.ConsoleRunner | 3.15.5 | 3.22.0 (has a `net10.0` agent) |
  | NUnit3TestAdapter | 3.17.0 | 6.3.1 (+ Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11.0) |
  | NUnit.Analyzers | – | 4.15.0 |
  | NLog | 5.0.1 | 6.2.2 |
  | Newtonsoft.Json | 13.0.3 | 13.0.4 |
  | CommandLineParser | 2.9.1 | 2.9.1 (latest) |
  | PowerShell hosting | Windows PowerShell 5.1 (GAC) | Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK 7.6.8 |
  | System.Management | .NET Framework | 10.0.13 package |

- **The 2,214 classic asserts** (`Assert.IsTrue`, `AreEqual`, `StringAssert`, `CollectionAssert`, …) are rewritten as `Assert.That` with constraints. In NUnit 4 and 5 that is the only built-in assertion model.
  - 20 assertions passed expected and actual in the wrong order; they now put the actual value first.
  - Four `Is.Not.Null.Or.Empty` checks only tested for null. They are now `Is.Not.Null.And.Not.Empty`.
  - Six format-string messages became interpolated strings.
- **The interop** is generated by `Tools/Interop.hMailServer.targets` instead of a `COMReference`. It uses the type library the installed server registered, or falls back to a local server build. The projects therefore also build with `dotnet build`.
- **Code pages:** .NET only ships the Unicode encodings by default. An assembly-wide `[SetUpFixture]` registers `CodePagesEncodingProvider` for the Windows-1252 messages the tests build. `API/Basics.cs`, the only Windows-1252 source file, is now UTF-8.
- **Packages restore into `hmailserver/test/packages/`.** CI and VMTestRunner find `nunit3-console.exe` there.
- **VMTestRunner** now copies the whole test build output to the guest, because a .NET test assembly needs its `.deps.json` and `.runtimeconfig.json` beside it. The guest gets the .NET runtime from the ArzoieMail setup.
- **`tests.yml`:** `nuget restore` is replaced by `msbuild /restore`, and the comments are updated.
- **Obsolete APIs** flagged by the .NET 10 build are replaced: `SHA1CryptoServiceProvider`, the `X509Certificate2` file constructor, and NLog's `Target.Register`.

## Verified locally

- The test solution builds with `dotnet build` and with Visual Studio's MSBuild (`/restore`, Debug and Release). There are no errors, and no warnings beyond the ones already present before this change.
- `nunit3-console --explore` loads `RegressionTests.dll` under the console runner's `net10.0` agent (CLR 10.0.13, NUnit 5.0.0). It discovers **1,294 test cases**, the same total as master's last run: 1,185 passed + 34 inconclusive + 75 skipped.
- Running a fixture without an installed server fails only at `new hMailServer.Application()` with "class not registered". That shows the runner and the interop work on .NET 10.

## Not verified

- **The full regression run** needs an installed server. The `Tests / Regression tests` check on this PR covers it, and should match the 1,185 / 0 / 34 / 75 baseline.
- **VMTestRunner against Hyper-V.** It builds and starts, but this machine has no Hyper-V. It now hosts PowerShell 7 rather than Windows PowerShell 5.1, so `Get-VM`, `Copy-VMFile` and PowerShell Direct need one run on a Hyper-V host.
